questions.prompt: How are high-voltage cables on a hybrid or electric vehicle usually identified?
questions.explanation: High-voltage cables and connectors are identified by orange insulation or conduit.

options.label: A
options.body: Blue insulation

options.label: B
options.body: Orange insulation or orange conduit

options.label: C
options.body: Green insulation

options.label: D
options.body: Plain black insulation with no marking

questions.prompt: What must be done before working near a high-voltage system?
questions.explanation: Isolate and power down following the manufacturer procedure, wear rated PPE, and verify the system is safe before work.

options.label: A
options.body: Just switch the ignition off and start work

options.label: B
options.body: Rev the engine to discharge the battery

options.label: C
options.body: Follow the manufacturer isolation procedure, wear rated PPE, and verify the system is powered down

options.label: D
options.body: Disconnect the 12-volt battery only, with no other checks

questions.prompt: Which gloves are required for high-voltage work?
questions.explanation: Electrically insulated gloves of the correct class, in test date, with leather over-gloves for protection.

options.label: A
options.body: Ordinary disposable workshop gloves

options.label: B
options.body: Electrically insulated gloves of the correct class, checked and in test date, with leather protectors

options.label: C
options.body: Heat-resistant welding gloves

options.label: D
options.body: No gloves, so you can feel components better

questions.prompt: Why should servicing follow the manufacturer schedule and specification?
questions.explanation: The manufacturer schedule uses the correct parts, fluids, and intervals, keeping the vehicle safe and protecting warranty.

options.label: A
options.body: It is only needed to keep a service stamp in the book

options.label: B
options.body: Any parts and fluids will do if they look similar

options.label: C
options.body: It keeps the vehicle safe and reliable and protects warranty, using the correct parts, fluids, and intervals

options.label: D
options.body: It lets you skip items that look clean

questions.prompt: When lifting a vehicle for servicing, you should:
questions.explanation: Use the specified lifting points, confirm the lift is secure, and use stands where required. Never rely on a jack alone.

options.label: A
options.body: Lift on any flat part of the floor pan

options.label: B
options.body: Use the manufacturer lifting points, check the lift is secure, and use stands where required

options.label: C
options.body: Work under a vehicle supported only by a jack

options.label: D
options.body: Lift as fast as possible to save time

questions.prompt: Before returning a serviced vehicle, the final checks should include:
questions.explanation: Final checks cover fluid levels, leaks, wheel nut torque, warning lights, and a road test where required.

options.label: A
options.body: Only washing the vehicle

options.label: B
options.body: Fluid levels, leaks, wheel nut torque, warning lights, and a road test where required

options.label: C
options.body: Resetting the trip meter only

options.label: D
options.body: Nothing, if no fault was reported

questions.prompt: A brake safety check should include:
questions.explanation: A brake check covers pedal feel, fluid, pads and discs, and hoses and lines for leaks or damage.

options.label: A
options.body: Pedal feel and travel, fluid level and condition, pad and disc condition, and hoses and lines for leaks or damage

options.label: B
options.body: Only whether the brake lights work

options.label: C
options.body: Only the handbrake holding on a hill

options.label: D
options.body: Only a visual look through the wheel spokes

questions.prompt: A tyre safety check should include:
questions.explanation: Check tread depth, pressures, cuts, bulges, uneven wear, and age or damage - including the spare where fitted.

options.label: A
options.body: Colour and brand only

options.label: B
options.body: Tread depth, pressures, cuts, bulges, uneven wear, and age or damage

options.label: C
options.body: Only whether the tyre holds air

options.label: D
options.body: Only the spare tyre

questions.prompt: During a safety check, lights and signalling should be checked for:
questions.explanation: All lamps, indicators, brake lights, and the horn must work, with no lens damage affecting output.

options.label: A
options.body: Brightness only

options.label: B
options.body: Operation of all lamps, indicators, brake lights, and the horn, plus lens damage

options.label: C
options.body: Headlamp aim only, with no bulb check

options.label: D
options.body: Nothing if the vehicle passed last time

questions.prompt: If a safety check finds a safety-critical defect, you should:
questions.explanation: Record and report safety-critical defects clearly and advise the vehicle should not be used until repaired.

options.label: A
options.body: Ignore it if the customer is in a hurry

options.label: B
options.body: Clear it without recording it

options.label: C
options.body: Record it clearly, report it, and advise that the vehicle should not be used until it is repaired

options.label: D
options.body: Mention it only if the customer asks

courses.title: Cooling System Servicing
moduleTitles: Best Practice Coolant Drain and Flush

questions.prompt: What does engine coolant do besides preventing freezing?
questions.explanation: Coolant raises the boiling point, lowers the freezing point, and carries corrosion inhibitors.

options.label: A
options.body: It raises the boiling point and contains corrosion inhibitors that protect the engine and radiator

options.label: B
options.body: It lubricates the water pump bearings only

options.label: C
options.body: It cleans the engine oil

options.label: D
options.body: Nothing - plain water does the same job in all conditions

questions.prompt: Why should different coolant types (for example OAT and older IAT types) generally not be mixed?
questions.explanation: Mixing different additive types can reduce protection and form deposits or gel. Use the specified type.

options.label: A
options.body: Mixing changes the colour only, with no other effect

options.label: B
options.body: The additives can react, reducing corrosion protection and forming deposits or gel

options.label: C
options.body: Mixing makes the coolant freeze-proof forever

options.label: D
options.body: Mixing is required at every service

questions.prompt: Which tool measures coolant freezing protection by how much the coolant bends light?
questions.explanation: A refractometer measures freeze protection from how the coolant bends light.

options.label: A
options.body: A multimeter

options.label: B
options.body: A refractometer

options.label: C
options.body: A torque wrench

options.label: D
options.body: A stethoscope

questions.prompt: Coolant test strips are mainly used to check:
questions.explanation: Test strips check freeze protection, pH, and remaining inhibitor (reserve alkalinity) level.

options.label: A
options.body: Tyre pressure and tread depth

options.label: B
options.body: Freeze protection, pH, and the remaining corrosion-inhibitor level

options.label: C
options.body: Engine oil viscosity

options.label: D
options.body: Battery voltage

questions.prompt: Best practice when draining and flushing a cooling system includes:
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Coolant Drain and Flush
questions.explanation: Work cold, catch and dispose of old coolant correctly, flush as directed, and refill with the correct coolant and mix.

options.label: A
options.body: Opening the cap on a hot engine to drain faster

options.label: B
options.body: Pouring old coolant down a drain

options.label: C
options.body: Working on a cold engine, catching and disposing of old coolant correctly, flushing as directed, and refilling with the correct coolant

options.label: D
options.body: Refilling with plain water only

questions.prompt: After refilling a cooling system, why must air be bled out correctly?
questions.moduleTitle: Best Practice Coolant Drain and Flush
questions.explanation: Trapped air causes overheating, poor heater output, and false temperature readings, so bleeding matters.

options.label: A
options.body: Air pockets can cause overheating, poor heater output, and false temperature readings

options.label: B
options.body: Air improves cooling, so it should be left in

options.label: C
options.body: Bleeding is only done for appearance

options.label: D
options.body: Air pockets only affect the air conditioning

questions.prompt: Most engine coolant temperature (ECT) sensors are NTC thermistors. This means their resistance:
questions.explanation: An NTC sensor's resistance falls as temperature rises.

options.label: A
options.body: Rises as temperature rises

options.label: B
options.body: Falls as temperature rises

options.label: C
options.body: Never changes

options.label: D
options.body: Is always zero

questions.prompt: An ECT sensor circuit reads a very cold temperature on a fully warmed engine. A likely cause is:
questions.explanation: An open or high-resistance circuit keeps signal voltage high, which the control unit reads as very cold.

options.label: A
options.body: A perfect sensor

options.label: B
options.body: Low tyre pressure

options.label: C
options.body: An open circuit or high resistance in the sensor or its wiring, keeping the signal voltage high

options.label: D
options.body: A new thermostat

questions.prompt: A drive belt should be replaced if inspection shows:
questions.explanation: Cracks, glazing, fraying, chunking, or oil/coolant contamination all mean the belt should be replaced.

options.label: A
options.body: Cracks, glazing, fraying, chunking, or contamination with oil or coolant

options.label: B
options.body: Only a little dust on the surface

options.label: C
options.body: The printed brand name has faded

options.label: D
options.body: Nothing - belts last the life of the vehicle

questions.prompt: A belt squeal on start-up most often points to:
questions.explanation: Start-up squeal usually means the belt is slipping: worn or glazed belt, weak tensioner, or misalignment.

options.label: A
options.body: A faulty spark plug

options.label: B
options.body: Low fuel level

options.label: C
options.body: A worn or glazed belt, weak tensioner, or pulley misalignment slipping under load

options.label: D
options.body: Worn brake pads

courses.title: Engine Oil Essentials
moduleTitles: Engine Oil Velocity and Performance Classifications
Engine Oil Basis Additives and Compositions

questions.prompt: What is the job of the bypass valve in an oil filter?
questions.explanation: The bypass valve opens if the filter blocks, so the engine still receives oil rather than none.

options.label: A
options.body: To stop all oil flow when the filter is new

options.label: B
options.body: To let oil bypass a blocked filter so the engine still gets oil, even if it is unfiltered

options.label: C
options.body: To increase oil pressure at idle only

options.label: D
options.body: To drain oil back to the sump overnight

questions.prompt: What does the anti-drainback valve in a filter prevent?
questions.explanation: The anti-drainback valve keeps oil in the filter and galleries when off, giving faster pressure on start-up.

options.label: A
options.body: Oil draining out of the filter and galleries when the engine is off, which would delay oil pressure on start-up

options.label: B
options.body: Fuel entering the oil

options.label: C
options.body: Coolant mixing with oil

options.label: D
options.body: Oil being filtered too well

questions.prompt: On a 5W-30 oil, what does the "5W" describe?
questions.moduleTitle: Engine Oil Velocity and Performance Classifications
questions.explanation: The number before W is the winter (cold) viscosity rating; 30 is the hot viscosity grade in 5W-30.

options.label: A
options.body: The oil's fuel economy rating

options.label: B
options.body: Its cold-temperature (winter) viscosity rating - how it flows when cold

options.label: C
options.body: The size of the container

options.label: D
options.body: The oil change interval in weeks

questions.prompt: Performance classifications such as API and ACEA categories tell you:
questions.moduleTitle: Engine Oil Velocity and Performance Classifications
questions.explanation: API / ACEA categories confirm the oil meets the performance level that engine and its emissions equipment require.

options.label: A
options.body: Only the colour of the oil

options.label: B
options.body: Whether the oil meets the required performance level for that engine type and emissions equipment

options.label: C
options.body: That any oil with a higher price is approved

options.label: D
options.body: Nothing - viscosity grade is the only thing that matters

questions.prompt: What do detergent and dispersant additives in engine oil do?
questions.moduleTitle: Engine Oil Basis Additives and Compositions
questions.explanation: Detergents clean surfaces; dispersants keep particles in suspension so the filter can trap them.

options.label: A
options.body: Make the oil foam on purpose

options.label: B
options.body: Wash the outside of the engine

options.label: C
options.body: Detergents clean deposits from surfaces and dispersants keep particles suspended so the filter can remove them

options.label: D
options.body: Replace the need for an oil filter

questions.prompt: Anti-wear additives such as ZDDP protect the engine mainly by:
questions.moduleTitle: Engine Oil Basis Additives and Compositions
questions.explanation: Anti-wear additives form a protective film on loaded metal surfaces where the oil film is thinnest.

options.label: A
options.body: Thickening the oil when hot

options.label: B
options.body: Forming a protective film on metal surfaces where the oil film is thinnest, such as cam lobes

options.label: C
options.body: Cooling the coolant

options.label: D
options.body: Sealing tyre punctures

questions.prompt: Compared with mineral oil, synthetic oil generally offers:
questions.explanation: Synthetic oil has more uniform molecules, with better cold flow and heat / oxidation resistance.

options.label: A
options.body: Worse cold starting flow

options.label: B
options.body: More uniform molecules, better cold flow, and better resistance to heat and oxidation

options.label: C
options.body: No difference at all

options.label: D
options.body: A shorter life in every engine

questions.prompt: Which statement about mineral oil is correct?
questions.explanation: Mineral oil is refined from crude, costs less, and is suitable where the manufacturer specifies it.

options.label: A
options.body: It is made in a laboratory with no crude oil involved in any grade

options.label: B
options.body: It never needs changing

options.label: C
options.body: It is refined from crude oil, costs less, and can be suitable where the manufacturer specifies it

options.label: D
options.body: It is always better than synthetic at high temperature

questions.prompt: When selecting engine oil for a service, the deciding source is:
questions.explanation: Always select by the manufacturer specification: viscosity grade plus the required approval / category.

options.label: A
options.body: Whatever oil is already open in the workshop

options.label: B
options.body: The manufacturer specification - viscosity grade and approval / performance category for that engine

options.label: C
options.body: The colour of the old oil

options.label: D
options.body: The cheapest oil on the shelf

questions.prompt: A vehicle used mainly for short trips should have its oil:
questions.explanation: Short trips contaminate oil with moisture and fuel and rarely get it fully hot - use the severe-service interval.

options.label: A
options.body: Changed less often, because the engine does fewer miles

options.label: B
options.body: Never changed if the level looks full

options.label: C
options.body: Topped up with any grade available

options.label: D
options.body: Changed on the severe-service schedule, because short trips cause moisture and fuel contamination and the oil rarely gets fully hot

courses.title: Transmission Servicing
moduleTitles: Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven Point Nine Transmission Service
VF Four Horsepower 16 Transmission Service Checks

questions.prompt: Why must the correct specified fluid be used in a 6-speed Hydramatic automatic?
questions.explanation: Fluid friction characteristics are matched to the clutches and shift calibration; wrong fluid causes shift faults.

options.label: A
options.body: Any automatic fluid shifts the same way

options.label: B
options.body: Friction characteristics are matched to the clutches and shift calibration - the wrong fluid can cause harsh or slipping shifts

options.label: C
options.body: Fluid type only affects the colour in the pan

options.label: D
options.body: The fluid is only there to cool the casing

questions.prompt: On many modern automatics with no dipstick, fluid level is checked by:
questions.explanation: With no dipstick, level is set at a specified fluid temperature using the level / overflow plug procedure.

options.label: A
options.body: Guessing from the amount drained out

options.label: B
options.body: Removing the wheels

options.label: C
options.body: Bringing the fluid to a specified temperature and checking flow from the level / overflow plug as directed

options.label: D
options.body: Overfilling, then driving until the excess escapes

questions.prompt: A Hydramatic pan service should include:
questions.explanation: Inspect pan and magnet, renew filter and gasket where specified, and refill with fresh specified fluid.

options.label: A
options.body: Reusing the old fluid to save cost

options.label: B
options.body: Inspecting the pan and magnet for debris, fitting a new filter and gasket where specified, and refilling with fresh specified fluid

options.label: C
options.body: Tightening pan bolts as tight as possible in any order

options.label: D
options.body: Skipping the filter if the fluid looks clean

questions.prompt: The Mercedes-Benz 722.9 (7G-Tronic) transmission fluid level is set by:
questions.moduleTitle: Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven Point Nine Transmission Service
questions.explanation: The 722.9 level is set by the overflow method at a specified temperature with approved-specification fluid only.

options.label: A
options.body: A conventional dipstick at any temperature

options.label: B
options.body: Filling until fluid pours out cold

options.label: C
options.body: Guesswork based on road feel

options.label: D
options.body: The overflow method at a specified fluid temperature, using only the approved-specification fluid

questions.prompt: Why is using only the approved fluid specification critical on the 722.9 service?
questions.moduleTitle: Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven Point Nine Transmission Service
questions.explanation: Unapproved fluid can upset friction and shift quality and may damage the transmission.

options.label: A
options.body: Unapproved fluid can upset shift quality and clutch friction and may damage the transmission

options.label: B
options.body: It only changes the service invoice wording

options.label: C
options.body: Any red automatic fluid is identical

options.label: D
options.body: Approved fluid is only needed under warranty for paperwork

questions.prompt: Debris on the pan magnet or in the filter during a transmission service tells you:
questions.moduleTitle: Mercedes-Benz Seven Seven Point Nine Transmission Service
questions.explanation: Heavy debris signals internal wear and needs further diagnosis, not just a fluid change.

options.label: A
options.body: Nothing - it should always be ignored

options.label: B
options.body: To add more fluid and return the vehicle

options.label: C
options.body: About internal wear - heavy friction material or metal can point to clutch or component wear that needs further diagnosis

options.label: D
options.body: That the fluid was overfilled at the factory

questions.prompt: On a wet-clutch VW / Audi DSG, routine service centres on:
questions.explanation: Wet-clutch DSG fluid cools and operates the clutches and mechatronics, so fluid and filter changes are scheduled service items.

options.label: A
options.body: Changing the DSG fluid and filter at the specified interval, because the fluid cools and operates the clutches and mechatronics

options.label: B
options.body: Never changing the fluid - it is sealed for life in all versions

options.label: C
options.body: Adjusting a clutch cable

options.label: D
options.body: Replacing the torque converter

questions.prompt: How is a DSG different from a conventional automatic?
questions.explanation: A DSG uses two clutches and two gear sets, preselecting the next gear, with no torque converter in most versions.

options.label: A
options.body: It has no gears at all

options.label: B
options.body: It uses two clutches and two gear sets, preselecting the next gear for very fast shifts, and has no torque converter in most versions

options.label: C
options.body: It is a manual gearbox with no electronics

options.label: D
options.body: It only works in reverse

questions.prompt: Transmission service checks on the ZF-type unit in this course should include:
questions.moduleTitle: VF Four Horsepower 16 Transmission Service Checks
questions.explanation: Service checks cover fluid level and condition, leaks, fault codes, cooler lines, and shift quality on road test.

options.label: A
options.body: Only a wash of the casing

options.label: B
options.body: Fluid level and condition, leaks, fault-code scan, cooler lines, and a road test of shift quality

options.label: C
options.body: Removing the transmission for every service

options.label: D
options.body: Checking only the engine oil

questions.prompt: Burnt-smelling, dark transmission fluid found during service checks most likely indicates:
questions.moduleTitle: VF Four Horsepower 16 Transmission Service Checks
questions.explanation: Burnt, dark fluid points to overheating and clutch wear; find the cause instead of only changing the fluid.

options.label: A
options.body: Normal fluid that needs no action

options.label: B
options.body: Too much coolant in the system

options.label: C
options.body: A recently changed filter

options.label: D
options.body: Overheating and clutch wear - the cause should be diagnosed, not just the fluid changed and returned
